newsitem.title: USA: Bolivia sells reconstituted crude for early May.
newsitem.headline: Bolivia sells reconstituted crude for early May.

text.p: Bolivia's state oil company sold 260,000 barrels of reconstituted crude oil to a U.S. trading company for loading around May 7-10, trade sources said on Wednesday.
Yacimientos Petroliferos Fiscales Bolivianos (YPFB) sold the crude at a discount of $5.95 a barrel to benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, the sources said.
YPFB held the tender on its own behalf, as well as in the name of equity producers YPF, Perez Companc, Tesoro and Ultramar/Diamond Shamrock.
The tender marked YPFB's second attempt to sell the crude. An earlier tender, which called for loading April 15, was canceled and reissued after the company received only one bid.
YPFB received two offers in the new tender.
Bolivia's reconstituted crude is mixed with gasoline to raise its API gravity to 45 degrees.
The crude loads at the Chilean port of Arica.
Bolivia holds crude tenders about every two months.
